newsitem.title: USA: Stadium bill affects local government power - PSA.
newsitem.headline: Stadium bill affects local government power - PSA.

text.p: A controversial stadiums bill proposed by U.S. Sen Daniel Patrick Moynihan, D-N.Y., may raise fundamental questions about who decides what is a governmental purpose concerning bond issues, a bond lobbyist said Wednesday.

Micah Green, executive vice president of Public Securities Association, said at the Grant's Municipal Bond Observer Fall Conference here that Moynihan's bill "is drawing a line" that can be redrawn over and over again by zealous legislators.
Moynihan's bill would eliminate tax-exempt financing for professional sports stadiums.
Green said the fundamental question the bill raises is not so much how stadiums should be financed but who decides what is an essential governmental purpose.
"What a governmental purpose is in a locality is a local perspective," Green said, noting that Moynihan's bill is an incursion into local government rights.
He said, "You have the federal government telling you what is an essential government purpose."
Green said, however, Moynihan has been a friend of municipal bonds in the past and his recent decision to change the effective date of the bill allows deals currently in the works to go forward.
As a result, Congress and the municipal market can go on to a more substantive discussion of the issue, Green said.
